definition.def: If you comment on something, you give your opinion about it or you give an explanation for it.
examples: So far, Mr Cook has not commented on these reports. [V on n/wh]
Stratford police refuse to comment on whether anyone has been arrested. [VERB + on]
You really can't comment till you know the facts. [VERB]
'I'm always happy with new developments,' he commented. [VERB with quote]
Stuart commented that this was very true. [VERB that]

definition.def: A comment is something that you say which expresses your opinion of something or which gives an explanation of it.
examples: He made his comments at a news conference in Amsterdam.
I was wondering whether you had any comments about that?
There's been no comment so far from police about the allegations.
The Prime Minister, who is abroad, was not available for comment.

definition.def: If an event or situation is a comment on something, it reveals something about that thing, usually something bad.
examples: He argues that family problems are typically a comment on some unresolved issues in the family. [+ on]

definition.def: People say 'no comment' as a way of refusing to answer a question, usually when it is asked by a journalist.
examples: No comment. I don't know anything.

examples.sentence: A survey conducted by Anthony Synott at Montreal's Concordia University asked participants to comment on how important smell was to them in their lives.
At the beginning, the pupils put solutions to the homework on the board, then the teachers comment, correct or elaborate as necessary.
I thought "How can I possibly do it? How can I comment on someone else's research when they probably spent 5 years doing it?"
OK, we'll have a careful look at the content of your case study in a minute, but I just want to make a general comment first, before you start writing your second draft.
You need to add some comment in that section about the implications of the figures.
